name: Bhoomi-Setu
summary: Bhoomi-Setu is a web app that helps check land records for problems. It compares details such as land area and the name of the holder across demo documents, and flags differences for a person to review. It can also read documents with an AI model, show the parcel on a map, and compare satellite-style images. Everything uses made-up demo data, not real government records. It also saves tamper-evident fingerprints of results so anyone can later check that a result was not altered.
who_its_for: People who want to understand or demo how land record mismatches could be found and explained, such as citizens, reviewers and evaluators. It is a prototype, so it is not clear it is meant for real use.
how_it_runs: It is a Next.js web app with pages in English and Hindi, and server code behind web addresses that store data in a local SQLite database or in Postgres. Automatic checks run on every push through a GitHub workflow, and the AI extraction needs keys set in the environment settings.

areas.name: src/app
areas.summary: Holds the web pages people see (case dashboard, documents, verification, review packet, public verify page) and the web addresses the server offers under api. It also holds the style files.
areas.why: This is where users and the server meet.
areas.debug_tips: For a wrong screen, check the page file under cases. For a wrong or missing data answer, check the matching route.ts and its test beside it.

areas.name: src/server
areas.summary: The core logic: creating cases, running verification checks, AI extraction, anchors, area comparison, review packets, mock government answers and the database layer. Most files have a test next to them.
areas.why: The real rules and decisions of the app live here.
areas.debug_tips: Start with the service for the feature that looks wrong, then run its test file. For storage trouble, look at database.ts.

areas.name: src/components
areas.summary: Reusable screen pieces: the page frame and navigation, the map, language and case holders, the earth observation and parcel panels, and decorative items like the globe and village drawing.
areas.why: They keep the look and shared state consistent across pages.
areas.debug_tips: For language or case loading problems, look at the locale and case context files. For map problems, look at parcel-map.tsx.

areas.name: docs
areas.summary: Contains a small Python lint tool under architecture-research that enforces project rules, such as no direct ownership transfers and no decimal numbers for land shares. It also has a script that checks the agent instruction file length.
areas.why: It guards the design promise that the app records evidence and never rewrites ownership.
areas.debug_tips: Run the lint command and read the printed violation codes and line numbers. The tests in the tests folder show what is flagged.

areas.name: src/lib
areas.summary: Helpers for display: all English and Hindi text, grouping of evidence, verification summaries, case loading status and the animated village scene.
areas.why: It turns raw data into what people read.
areas.debug_tips: For odd or missing wording, check i18n.ts. For wrong grouping or counts, check the presentation files and their tests.

areas.name: (root files)
areas.summary: Project setup files: the package manifest, TypeScript, ESLint, Next.js and Vitest settings, and the environment template. The next-env.d.ts file is generated and should not be edited.
areas.why: They define how the app is installed, built, tested and configured.
areas.debug_tips: For build or startup trouble, check package.json commands and that .env values are filled in from .env.example.

areas.name: src/types
areas.summary: Type definitions describing the shapes of cases, anchors, imagery and map geometry.
areas.why: They give the whole codebase one shared vocabulary.
areas.debug_tips: When data seems to have the wrong fields, compare it with the matching type file.

areas.name: src/evaluation
areas.summary: A fixed set of twelve synthetic land cases with scoring rules and tests that check every verification check gives the right result.
areas.why: It shows whether the verification logic stays correct.
areas.debug_tips: If an evaluation test fails, read its printed summary to see which case was scored wrong.

areas.name: src/services
areas.summary: Browser-side client code that asks the server for cases, plus a document text parser and an in-memory demo case store. How these are used relative to the server code is not fully clear from the summaries.
areas.why: It connects the screens to case data.
areas.debug_tips: If case data fails to load, check case-service.ts first. For wrong parsed fields such as khata number or area, check document-processing.ts.

areas.name: scripts
areas.summary: Two helper scripts: one takes screenshots of the live demo, the other edits a stored record to show how tampering is detected, and can undo the edit.
areas.why: They support demos and show the anchor feature working.
areas.debug_tips: Run the tamper demo against a local database only. If screenshots fail, check that the demo site is reachable.

areas.name: .github
areas.summary: One workflow file that runs automatic checks on every push and pull request.
areas.why: It catches broken code before it is merged.
areas.debug_tips: Open the failed run in GitHub and compare the failing step with the same command in package.json.

readiness.summary: Top fixes: add logging and error tracking, scan git history for secrets and run tests plus `npm audit` to confirm they pass, and strengthen input validation on API routes and uploads. Also add a rollback procedure and a clear install-and-start sequence to the docs.

checks.question: Does the app build and start with one documented command?
checks.evidence: `package.json` has `dev`, `build`, `start` scripts and the `README.md` documents `npm run dev` with a `package-lock.json` present. Build was not run, and the README excerpt does not show a single install-and-start sequence or required env setup.
checks.next_step: Add a Quick Start block to `README.md` with `npm ci`, copy `.env.example`, `npm run dev`.

checks.question: Are there automated tests, and do they pass?
checks.evidence: Not checked: tests were not run in this pass. 46 test files exist (e.g. `src/app/api/anchors/verify.test.ts`), `package.json` has `test` and `eval` scripts, and `.github/workflows/ci.yml` exists, but pass status is unverified. Some test files are in `docs/architecture-research/` (Python) with no Python deps listed.
checks.next_step: Run `npm test` and check the latest CI run result.

checks.question: When something goes wrong, does the app show a clear message instead of crashing or failing silently?
checks.evidence: Not checked: the static scan found 0 swallowed-error patterns, but no evidence of error boundaries, `error.tsx` files or API error response shapes was provided. The README describes `INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE` as a verification outcome, which is a good sign but not error handling.
checks.next_step: Confirm `error.tsx`/`not-found.tsx` exist and API routes return structured error JSON.

checks.question: Does it check what people type or upload before using it?
checks.evidence: Input validation patterns appear in only 5 matches across 4 files, which is thin for an app with API routes and document handling. Coverage of upload and case-ID inputs is not shown.
checks.next_step: Add schema validation (e.g. zod) to every API route and any upload endpoint, with size and type limits.

checks.question: Are passwords and API keys kept out of the code and out of git history?
checks.evidence: Only `.env.example` is tracked, `.gitignore` mentions `.env`, and 0 secret-looking strings were found in HEAD. Git history was not scanned, so past leaks are not ruled out.
checks.next_step: Run a history scan (gitleaks or trufflehog) given the full preserved history, including the earlier project's commits.

checks.question: Can only the right people see and change things (sign-in and permissions)?
checks.evidence: 21 auth/session/permission matches in 14 files suggest some access logic exists. The product is a synthetic-data demo with a public deployment, and per-user roles are not evidenced.
checks.next_step: Document the intended access model; if real data is ever used, add sign-in and per-case authorization.

checks.question: Is important data backed up, and are database changes made through migrations?
checks.evidence: No migrations folder was found and no backup procedure is evidenced. The app appears to use synthetic fixtures rather than a database, so this matters mainly if real data is introduced.
checks.next_step: State in `docs/DATA_MODEL.md` that data is synthetic and static; add migrations and backups before any persistent store is used.

checks.question: Are third-party packages reasonably up to date and free of known security problems?
checks.evidence: Not checked: the dependency audit was not run. A `package-lock.json` is present, which makes an audit possible, but versions and advisories were not examined.
checks.next_step: Run `npm audit` and enable Dependabot or Renovate.

checks.question: If it breaks while people use it, will logs or alerts show what happened?
checks.evidence: The static scan found 0 logging matches in 0 files. No logger, error tracker or alerting configuration is evident.
checks.next_step: Add structured server-side logging in API routes and connect an error tracker such as Sentry or Vercel log drains.

checks.question: Does it stay fast with realistic amounts of data and users?
checks.evidence: Not checked: no load or performance testing was run, and nothing in the evidence shows benchmarks. Synthetic demo data is small by design.
checks.next_step: Add a basic load test or Lighthouse check on the hero case and key API routes.

checks.question: Is there a written, repeatable way to deploy it and to roll back a bad release?
checks.evidence: `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` exists, `.github/workflows/ci.yml` is present, and the README links a Vercel deployment. A rollback procedure is not evidenced in the excerpt.
checks.next_step: Add a rollback section to `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` (e.g. Vercel instant rollback to a prior deployment).

checks.question: Could someone new run it and understand it from the docs alone?
checks.evidence: `README.md` explains purpose, demo flow, and provenance, and `docs/` includes `API.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `DATA_MODEL.md`, `DEPLOYMENT.md`, `DOCUMENT_PIPELINE.md`, `EARTH_OBSERVATION.md`, `EVALUATION.md` and `DEMO_SCRIPT.md`.

readiness.method: Static evidence only; tests, build and audit were not run in this pass.

debug_playbook.symptom: A case page shows loading forever or an error
steps: Check that the case ID in the web address exists.
Open the case route in the browser and see whether it returns data or an error.
Check the health address to confirm the database responds.

debug_playbook.symptom: Verification results look wrong or missing
steps: Confirm the case has its documents attached.
Compare the saved results with the evaluation cases.

debug_playbook.symptom: Document extraction says unavailable or fails
steps: Check that an AI provider key is set in the environment.
Confirm the document is an approved synthetic one.
Read the saved failure record for the reason.

debug_playbook.symptom: A public verify page shows a mismatch
steps: Check whether the tamper demo was run and not undone.
Compare the stored fingerprint with the recalculated one.

debug_playbook.symptom: Text appears in the wrong language
steps: Check that the text exists in both English and Hindi.
Clear the saved language in the browser and reload.

glossary.meaning: A saved, tamper-evident record of a verification result, tied to a fingerprint (hash) so changes can be detected.
Automatic checks that compare area and holder name across documents and flag differences.
Made-up demo records used instead of real land or personal data.
A draft summary of a case's potential issues prepared for a human reviewer.
One piece of land, shown on a map with its boundary and area.
Indian land record terms for an account number and a revenue village. Their exact use here is not spelled out.
Using an AI model to pull facts out of a document, accepted only if backed by an exact quote.
Two demo cases: one with planted discrepancies and one without, to show no false alarms.
Satellite-style before and after imagery, here made up, showing changes like vegetation.
A stand-in for a government data source that returns fixed, labelled synthetic answers.
